cases.description: check_old_code/1 answers false for a module with no old-code version
cases.eval: try (begin code:ensure_loaded(lists), erlang:check_old_code(lists) end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:display/1 writes an atom and an integer bare through the C `%T` printer, one `\r\n`-terminated line per call, and the probe's own line follows them
cases.eval: try (begin erlang:display(hello), erlang:display(42), done end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:display/1 renders a printable binary in its quoted `<<"…">>` form and a binary with a non-printable byte in the numbered `<<1,2,255>>` form
cases.eval: try (begin erlang:display(<<"bin">>), erlang:display(<<1,2,255>>), done end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:display/1 renders a float with the `%T` printer's `%e` shape (`1.500000e+00`, not `1.5`) and a negative integer with its sign
cases.eval: try (begin erlang:display(1.5), erlang:display(-42), done end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:display/1 renders an all-printable list as its quoted string form (`"hi"`) and an improper list elementwise with the `|` tail marker
cases.eval: try (begin erlang:display([104,105]), erlang:display([1,2,3|tail]), done end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:display/1's `%T` printer has no `~p`-style depth or length limit: a seven-deep tuple and a list with a non-printable element both render in full
cases.eval: try (begin erlang:display({1,{2,{3,{4,{5,{6,{7,8}}}}}}}), erlang:display([97,98,300]), done end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:display/1 quotes an atom that is not a plain lowercase name (`'hello world'`) and renders the empty tuple as `{}`
cases.eval: try (begin erlang:display('hello world'), erlang:display({}), done end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:display/1 answers the atom `true` (not the term), so two calls in one expression render both lines and yield `{true,true}`
cases.eval: try ({erlang:display(one), erlang:display(two)}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:display/1 renders a tuple elementwise and quotes a printable list element (`"s"`), while the empty list stays `[]`
cases.eval: try (begin erlang:display({a,1,"s",[]}), done end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: fun_info/2's env of a local fun lists the captured value it closed over
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:fun_captured_env()]), halt(0).

cases.description: fun_info/2's env of a local fun that captures nothing is the empty list
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:fun_local_env()]), halt(0).

cases.description: fun_info/2 of a compiled local fun answers all four identity items (module, name, arity, type)
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:fun_local_items()]), halt(0).

cases.description: a local fun's index and new_index are 0 (its fun-table slot) and its uniq/new_uniq are the compiler's hash shapes — integer and 16 bytes — not literals
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:fun_local_index_items()]), halt(0).

cases.description: fun_info/2's pid item of a local fun is tagged `pid` and holds the creating process's pid (classified, never rendered: a pid is per-VM-start)
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:fun_pid_item()]), halt(0).

cases.description: the whole ten-key fun_info/1 proplist of a compiled local fun, with only the volatile and hash values classified
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:fun_whole_list()]), halt(0).

cases.description: function_exported/3 answers true for an exported function and false for an unexported one once the module is explicitly loaded
cases.eval: try (begin code:ensure_loaded(lists), {erlang:function_exported(lists, reverse, 1), erlang:function_exported(lists, no_such_fun, 0)} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:get_module_info/2 (the deprecated module_info/1 alias) answers the module name of the erlang module
cases.eval: try (erlang:get_module_info(erlang, module)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: is_builtin/3 answers true for a declared erlang:* BIF and false for an undeclared name
cases.eval: try ({erlang:is_builtin(erlang, self, 0), erlang:is_builtin(erlang, not_a_bif, 0)}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: Module:module_info(attributes) of a compiled module carries exactly the compiler-added `vsn` attribute, as an integer (the md5 itself is compiler-version-derived, so only its presence and type are pinned)
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:mod_info(2)]), halt(0).

cases.description: Module:module_info(exports) of a freshly erlc-compiled module is the sorted export table plus module_info/0,1
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:mod_info(0)]), halt(0).

cases.description: Module:module_info(module) of a compiled module answers its (atom) module name
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:mod_info(1)]), halt(0).

cases.description: process_info/2 and process_info/1 answer the atom `undefined` for a pid that is no longer in the process table (never an empty list)
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_dead()]), halt(0).

cases.description: process_info/2's dictionary item lists a spawned process's stored pairs (sorted: the oracle's own order is a per-VM hash order) and the {dictionary,Key} item answers the stored value or `undefined`
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_dict()]), halt(0).

cases.description: process_info/2's garbage_collection_info item is the eleven-pair proplist in the emulator's documented order with an integer value per key (the figures themselves are per-VM and never pinned)
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> {garbage_collection_info, Info} = erlang:process_info(self(), garbage_collection_info), {length(Info), [K || {K, _} <- Info], [is_integer(Val) || {_, Val} <- Info]} end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: process_info/2 with an item *list* answers in the requested order and repeats a duplicated item
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_list_order()]), halt(0).

cases.description: process_info/2's label item is `undefined` for a process that never set one and answers the value put under the '$process_label' dictionary key
cases.eval: try ({erlang:process_info(self(), label), begin put('$process_label', my_label), erlang:process_info(self(), label) end}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: last_calls of an armed parked child — queried from its parent, so the query itself is the parent's call — is a ring holding the child's `Parent ! ready` send, both as the {erlang,send,2} triple and as the bare `send` pseudo entry, and every entry is an {M,F,A} triple or one of send/'receive'/timeout (the ring's exact contents are a documented superset of the oracle's, so they are never pinned)
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_last_calls_ring()]), halt(0).

cases.description: last_calls has three states — `false` unarmed, a *list* while process_flag (save_calls, N) is armed and `false` again after the save_calls, 0 disarm — and process_flag(save_calls, N) answers the previous ring size, refusing 10001 and -1 with error:badarg (the armed ring's contents are a superset of the oracle's, so only its list-ness is pinned)
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> Unarmed = erlang:process_info(self(), last_calls), Prev = process_flag(save_calls, 10), {last_calls, Armed} = erlang:process_info(self(), last_calls), Prev2 = process_flag(save_calls, 0), After = erlang:process_info(self(), last_calls), Bad = [try process_flag(save_calls, N) of Back -> Back catch Cls:Rs -> {Cls, Rs} end || N <- [10001, -1, 10000]], {Unarmed, Prev, is_list(Armed), Prev2, After, Bad} end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: process_info/2's links item follows link/1 and unlink/1 on a spawned process
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_links()]), halt(0).

cases.description: process_info/2's magic_ref item is the empty list in both the atom form and the item-list form (the /2 atom form is deliberately unwrapped)
cases.eval: try ({erlang:process_info(self(), magic_ref), erlang:process_info(self(), [magic_ref])}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: process_info/2's message_queue_len and messages report a spawned process's queued payloads, in FIFO order
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_messages()]), halt(0).

cases.description: the monitored_by item of a monitored process and the monitors item of the monitor both report the {process,_} pair (counted, never rendered: a pid is volatile)
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_monitors()]), halt(0).

cases.description: process_info/2's parent item is the `init` process for the `-eval` root (so it is never the process itself) and the *spawner* for a spawned child (classified into booleans: a pid is per-VM-start)
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> {parent, Root} = erlang:process_info(self(), parent), RootIsInit = Root =:= whereis(init), RootIsSelf = element(2, erlang:process_info(self(), parent)) =:= self(), Parent = self(), P = spawn(fun() -> Parent ! ready, receive stop -> ok end end), ready = receive ready -> ready after 2000 -> timeout end, {parent, Spawner} = erlang:process_info(P, parent), {RootIsInit, RootIsSelf, Spawner =:= Parent, Spawner =:= P} end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: process_info/2's priority_messages item is the boolean `false` for a plain process — a boolean, never a 0/1 integer
cases.eval: try ({erlang:process_info(self(), priority_messages), is_boolean(element(2, erlang:process_info(self(), priority_messages))), is_integer(element(2, erlang:process_info(self(), priority_messages)))}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: an unknown item name, a first argument that is not a pid and a non-atom/non-list item all raise error:badarg
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_badarg()]), halt(0).

cases.description: process_info/1 of a registered spawned process prepends registered_name to the 16-key set
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_registered_keys()]), halt(0).

cases.description: process_info(self(), dictionary) lists the calling process's stored pair (a single entry, so its order is vacuous)
cases.eval: try (begin put(diff_k, diff_v), erlang:process_info(self(), dictionary) end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: process_info/2's last_calls of a process with no saved-calls buffer is the atom `false` — both for the default (never armed) state and after an explicit process_flag(save_calls, 0) disarm
cases.eval: try ({erlang:process_info(self(), last_calls), begin process_flag(save_calls, 0), erlang:process_info(self(), last_calls) end}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: current_function, initial_call and status of the *running* `-eval` process: the evaluator's own frame, the root apply/2 initial call and the `running` status
cases.eval: try ({erlang:process_info(self(), current_function), erlang:process_info(self(), initial_call), erlang:process_info(self(), status)}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the *list* form of process_info/2 wraps registered_name — {registered_name,[]} for an unregistered process — and reports status alongside it
cases.eval: try (erlang:process_info(self(), [registered_name, status])) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: process_info(self(), registered_name) of an unregistered process is the bare empty list (the /2 atom form is deliberately unwrapped)
cases.eval: try (erlang:process_info(self(), registered_name)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: process_info(self(), trap_exit) tracks process_flag(trap_exit, _) in both directions
cases.eval: try (begin process_flag(trap_exit, true), T = erlang:process_info(self(), trap_exit), process_flag(trap_exit, false), {T, erlang:process_info(self(), trap_exit)} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: process_info/1 of the running process is the same fixed 16-key set in the emulator's own order (registered_name omitted while unregistered)
cases.eval: try ([K || {K, _} <- erlang:process_info(self())]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: current_location of a spawned process names module/function/arity and carries the {file,_}/{line,_} location list, the line being the parked child's own source line
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_location()]), halt(0).

cases.description: current_stacktrace of a spawned process is the single innermost frame, with a two-entry location list
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_stack()]), halt(0).

cases.description: the twenty process_info/2 items whose value of a spawned parked process is exactly the oracle's (the mailbox, the flags, the emulator's heap policy, the trace state)
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_exact()]), halt(0).

cases.description: the widest process_info/2 item set — all 31 items — is answered for a spawned process with the oracle's value kind (an internal quantity is a kind, not a value)
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_shape()]), halt(0).

cases.description: process_info/1 of an unregistered spawned process is the fixed 16-key set in the emulator's own order (registered_name is omitted)
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_keys()]), halt(0).

cases.description: process_info/2 of a spawned parked process answers current_function, initial_call, catchlevel and status — the ledger's `unsupported` position items now resolve
cases.eval: io:format("~w~n",[diff_bif_extra:pi_position()]), halt(0).

cases.description: erts_internal:term_to_string/2 takes a byte budget: an affordable term still gains the `"... "` marker, a tight budget truncates mid-term, and `undefined` / `INT_MAX-1` are the unlimited arms
cases.eval: try ([erts_internal:term_to_string({a,1}, B) =:= S || {B,S} <- [{4,"{a,1}... "},{2,"{a... "},{undefined,"{a,1}"},{2147483646,"{a,1}"}]]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erts_internal:term_to_string/2's argument check accepts only `1 < Limit < INT_MAX` or the atom `undefined`, so 1, 0, -1, `INT_MAX` itself and a non-integer limit all raise error:badarg
cases.eval: try ([try erts_internal:term_to_string({a,1}, L) of _ -> ok catch Cls:Rs -> {Cls, Rs} end || L <- [1, 0, -1, 2147483647, foo]]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erts_internal:term_to_string/1 answers a character list (a list, never a binary) holding the `%T` rendering — `{a,1}` renders the five bytes `"{a,1}"`
cases.eval: try ({is_list(erts_internal:term_to_string({a,1})), is_binary(erts_internal:term_to_string({a,1})), erts_internal:term_to_string({a,1})}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erts_internal:term_to_string/0 is no exported function, so the call raises the oracle's bare error:undef
cases.eval: try (try erts_internal:term_to_string() of _ -> ok catch Cls:Rs -> {Cls, Rs} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erts_internal:term_to_string/1 renders a float, a map, a printable list and a printable binary exactly like the `%T` printer (the expected strings are the oracle's measured renderings)
cases.eval: try ([erts_internal:term_to_string(T) =:= S || {T,S} <- [{1.5,"1.500000e+00"},{#{a=>1},"#{a=>1}"},{"hello","\"hello\""},{<<"xy">>,"<<\"xy\">>"}]]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:apply/2,3 on a module and a fun, split_binary/2, binary_to_list/1 and list_to_binary/1
cases.eval: try ({erlang:apply(lists, reverse, [[1,2]]), erlang:apply(fun(X) -> X+1 end, [1]), erlang:split_binary(<<1,2,3>>, 2), erlang:binary_to_list(<<1,2>>), list_to_binary([1,2])}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: binary_to_atom/2 with utf8, atom_to_binary/2 round trip, latin1 and the list forms
cases.eval: try ({binary_to_atom(<<"hello">>, utf8), atom_to_binary(binary_to_atom(<<195,169>>, utf8), utf8), atom_to_binary(ok, latin1), list_to_atom("hello"), atom_to_list(hello)}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: atom_to_binary/1 renders the atom as a UTF-8 binary
cases.eval: try (atom_to_binary(hello)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: base64:encode/1 of a zero-length binary is the zero-length binary <<>>
cases.eval: try (base64:encode(binary:copy(<<$A>>, 0))) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: beam_lib:md5/1 hashes a loaded module's .beam image into a 16-byte digest
cases.eval: try (begin {ok,{lists,Digest}} = beam_lib:md5(code:which(lists)), {is_binary(Digest), byte_size(Digest)} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: binary:decode_unsigned/1 reads a big-endian unsigned integer
cases.eval: try (binary:decode_unsigned(<<1,2>>)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: binary:encode_unsigned/1 is the inverse of decode_unsigned/1
cases.eval: try (binary:encode_unsigned(258)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: binary:part/3 extracts a sub-binary
cases.eval: try (binary:part(<<1,2,3,4>>, 1, 2)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: binary:part/2,3, first/1, last/1, at/2 and copy/2
cases.eval: try ({binary:part(<<"hello">>, 1, 3), binary:part(<<"hello">>, {1,3}), binary:first(<<"ab">>), binary:last(<<"ab">>), binary:at(<<"ab">>, 1), binary:copy(<<"ab">>, 3)}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: binary:replace/3,4, encode_unsigned/1,2 (big/little), decode_unsigned/1,2 and bin_to_list/list_to_bin
cases.eval: try ({binary:replace(<<"hello">>, <<"l">>, <<"L">>), binary:replace(<<"hello">>, <<"l">>, <<"L">>, [global]), binary:encode_unsigned(300), binary:encode_unsigned(300, little), binary:decode_unsigned(<<1,44>>), binary:decode_unsigned(<<44,1>>, little), binary:bin_to_list(<<"ab">>), binary:list_to_bin([1,2])}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: binary:split/2,3 (with `global`), match/2, matches/2 and longest_common_prefix/suffix/1
cases.eval: try ({binary:split(<<"a,b,c">>, <<",">>), binary:split(<<"a,b,c">>, <<",">>, [global]), binary:match(<<"hello">>, <<"ll">>), binary:matches(<<"hello">>, <<"l">>), binary:longest_common_prefix([<<"ab">>, <<"ac">>]), binary:longest_common_suffix([<<"ab">>, <<"cb">>])}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: byte_size/1 reports the size of a binary in bytes
cases.eval: try (byte_size(<<1,2,3>>)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: erlang:cancel_timer/1 is false for a timer that never existed
cases.eval: try (erlang:cancel_timer(make_ref())) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: code:purge/1 guards on is_atom/1 in code.erl, so a non-atom is the bare error:function_clause
cases.eval: try (code:purge(42)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the purge queries answer the same no-old-code pair for a module that was never loaded
cases.eval: try ({code:purge(nosuchmod), code:soft_purge(nosuchmod)}) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: code:purge/1 answers false and code:soft_purge/1 true for a loaded module with no old code
cases.eval: try (begin {module,lists} = code:ensure_loaded(lists), {code:purge(lists), code:soft_purge(lists)} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: code:soft_purge/1 carries the same is_atom/1 guard, so a non-atom is error:function_clause too

cases.eval: try ([bit_size(<<1,2,3>>), byte_size(<<1,2,3>>), bit_size(<<1:1>>), bit_size(<<>>), byte_size(<<>>), begin try bit_size(1234) catch error:SReason -> SReason end end, begin try byte_size(1234) catch error:TReason -> TReason end end]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a little-endian segment past 60 bits is a bignum write: its low bits land first, the rest above
cases.eval: try ([<<(1 bsl 60):60/little>>, <<(1 bsl 64):72/little>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the binary16 segment's subnormal, overflow-to-infinity and negative-zero images
cases.eval: try ([<<0.1:16/float>>, <<3.14159:16/float>>, <<70000.0:16/float>>, <<1.0e10:16/float>>, <<5.0e-8:16/float>>, <<-0.0:16/float>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a binary16 segment rounds an exact tie to the even mantissa, in both directions
cases.eval: try ([<<(1.0 + 1.0/2048):16/float>>, <<(1.0 + 3.0/2048):16/float>>, <<(1.0 + 1.0/2048):32/float>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the binary32/binary64 float segments, big- and little-endian, from a float and an integer value
cases.eval: try ([<<1.5:32/float>>, <<1.5:32/float-little>>, <<1.0e40:64/float>>, <<1.0e40:32/float>>, <<3.14159:32/float>>, <<(1 bsl 64):64/float>>, <<1.5/float>>, <<1.5/float-little>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a float segment whose width is not 16/32/64 bits (or whose value is not a number) is badarg
cases.eval: try ([begin try <<1.5:8/float>> catch error:W1 -> W1 end end, begin try <<1.5:24/float>> catch error:W2 -> W2 end end, begin try <<1.5:128/float>> catch error:W3 -> W3 end end, begin try <<foo/float>> catch error:W4 -> W4 end end]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the byte-aligned little-endian forms (explicit size, unit:8 and 16/32-bit) are the byte reversal
cases.eval: try ([<<16#1234:2/little-unit:8>>, <<1:2/unit:8>>, <<256:2/unit:8>>, <<256:16/little>>, <<16#1234:16/little>>, <<16#1234:32/little>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a little-endian field narrower than a byte, and one starting at a bit offset, keep the field's low bits
cases.eval: try ([<<16#1234:4/little>>, <<16#1234:5/little>>, <<1:1,16#1234:12/little>>, <<-1:12/little>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a little-endian segment writes its whole bytes first and the trailing partial field above them
cases.eval: try ([<<-300:12/little>>, <<16#1234:12/little>>, <<256:9/little>>, <<255:12/little>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a total size that is not a whole number of bytes is a non-byte-aligned bit string
cases.eval: try ([<<1,2,3:5>>, bit_size(<<1,2,3:5>>), <<1:4,2:8,3:4>>, <<1:3,2:7>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a string literal is one segment per character, and the utf types encode each character
cases.eval: try ([<<"abc">>, <<"abc":16>>, <<"abc"/utf8>>, <<"abc"/utf16>>, <<"abc"/utf16-little>>, <<"abc"/utf32>>, <<>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a big-endian integer segment truncates to its low Size bits in two's complement, at any width
an unsized binary/bitstring segment splices its value's bits in place, at any alignment
cases.eval: try ([<<(<<1,2,3>>)/binary>>, <<1,(<<2,3>>)/binary>>, <<(<<1:1>>)/bitstring,(<<0:7>>)/bitstring>>, <<(<<1:4>>)/bitstring,2:4>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a utf16 segment emits a surrogate pair past 16#FFFF (big- and little-endian, native)
cases.eval: try ([<<16#41/utf16>>, <<16#41/utf16-little>>, <<16#41/utf16-native>>, <<16#7FF/utf16>>, <<16#10000/utf16>>, <<16#10FFFF/utf16>>, <<16#10000/utf16-little>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a utf32 segment is one 4-byte code point in either byte order
cases.eval: try ([<<1234/utf32>>, <<1234/utf32-little>>, <<16#10000/utf32>>, <<16#10FFFF/utf32>>, <<0/utf32>>, <<16#10000/utf32-little>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a utf8 segment encodes 1..4 bytes by code-point range
cases.eval: try ([<<16#41/utf8>>, <<16#7FF/utf8>>, <<16#20AC/utf8>>, <<16#10FFFF/utf8>>, <<16#10000/utf8>>]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a surrogate, an out-of-range or negative code point, and a non-integer value are badarg on every utf segment
cases.eval: try ([begin try <<16#D800/utf16>> catch error:U1 -> U1 end end, begin try <<16#110000/utf16>> catch error:U2 -> U2 end end, begin try <<16#D800/utf32>> catch error:U3 -> U3 end end, begin try <<16#110000/utf32>> catch error:U4 -> U4 end end, begin try <<-1/utf8>> catch error:U5 -> U5 end end, begin try <<16#D800/utf8>> catch error:U6 -> U6 end end, begin try <<atom/utf16>> catch error:U7 -> U7 end end, begin try <<[1040]/utf16>> catch error:U8 -> U8 end end]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a float pattern width that is not 16/32/64 bits is a match failure, never a raise
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<1.5:64/float>> of <<F:16/float>> -> F; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0>> of <<F:24/float,Rest/binary>> -> {F,Rest}; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<0,0,0,0>> of <<F:24/float>> -> F; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<0,0,0>> of <<F:32/float>> -> F; _ -> nomatch end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a float pattern segment decodes the IEEE field at 16/32/64 bits, reversed by little/native
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<1.5:16/float>> of <<F:16/float>> -> F end end, fun() -> case <<0,62>> of <<F:16/float>> -> F end end, fun() -> case <<1.5:32/float>> of <<F:32/float>> -> F end end, fun() -> case <<1.5:32/float>> of <<F:32/float-little>> -> F end end, fun() -> case <<1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8>> of <<F:16/float,Rest/binary>> -> {F,Rest} end end, fun() -> case <<1.5/float>> of <<F/float>> -> F end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a little-endian pattern segment reads the whole bytes first and the trailing partial field above them
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<212,14:4>> of <<A:12/little>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<212,14:4>> of <<A:12/signed-little>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<0,1:1>> of <<A:9/little>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<1,2,3>> of <<A:24/little>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<255,255>> of <<A:16/signed-little>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<10:4>> of <<A:4/little>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<-300:12/little>> of <<A:12/little>> -> A end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the little-endian reader is exact past a word and off byte alignment, signed and unsigned
signed sign-extends within the segment width (12, 60 and 64 bits) and leaves the unsigned read alone
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<255,255,255,255,255,255,255,255>> of <<A:64/signed>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<16#80,0,0,0,0,0,0,0>> of <<A:64/signed>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<(1 bsl 59):60>> of <<A:60/signed>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<(1 bsl 59):60>> of <<A:60>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<255,15:4>> of <<A:12/signed>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<2,2:4>> of <<A:12/signed>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<16#7FF:12>> of <<A:12/signed>> -> A end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: an integer pattern segment reads any width exactly, incl. 72/120-bit bignum fields
a zero-width field matches empty, and fields read correctly from a non-byte-aligned subject
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<>> of <<A:0>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<1:1,16#12,16#34>> of <<_:1,A:16>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<1:1,16#12,16#34>> of <<_:1,A:8,Rest/binary>> -> {A,Rest} end end, fun() -> case <<0:4,(<<255:12/little>>)/bitstring>> of <<_:4,A:12/little>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<0:4,(<<3796:12>>)/bitstring>> of <<_:4,A:12/little>> -> A; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<1:3,16#12,16#34>> of <<_:1,A:2,_/bitstring>> -> A end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a lone high/low surrogate and a mis-ordered pair are a match failure, never a raise
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<16#D8,0>> of <<C/utf16>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<16#DC,0>> of <<C/utf16>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<16#D8,0,16#41,0>> of <<C/utf16>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<255,255,219,255>> of <<C/utf16-little>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<255,223,255,219>> of <<C/utf16-little>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: an overlong, surrogate, out-of-range or truncated UTF-8 sequence is a match failure
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<16#C0,16#80>> of <<C/utf8>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<16#FF>> of <<C/utf8>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<16#ED,16#A0,16#80>> of <<C/utf8>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<16#E2,16#82>> of <<C/utf8>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<16#E2,16#41,16#AC>> of <<C/utf8>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<16#F4,16#90,16#80,16#80>> of <<C/utf8>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a non-byte-aligned subject matches integer fields and an empty rest at its own alignment
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<1,2,3:5>> of <<A:8,B:8,C:5>> -> {A,B,C} end end, fun() -> case <<>> of <<>> -> empty end end, fun() -> case <<1:3,2:7>> of <<A:10>> -> A end end, fun() -> N = 12, case <<212,14:4>> of <<A:N/little>> -> A end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a string literal in a pattern is one 8-bit segment per character
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<"abc">> of <<"abc">> -> yes; _ -> no end end, fun() -> case <<65,66,67>> of <<"ABC">> -> yes; _ -> no end end, fun() -> case <<1,"abc">> of <<X:8,"abc">> -> X end end, fun() -> case <<97,98>> of <<"abc">> -> yes; _ -> no end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a pattern field needing more bits than the subject holds is a match failure, never badarg
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<1,2,3>> of <<A:32>> -> A; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<1,2,3>> of <<A:24>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<1,2,3:5>> of <<A:24>> -> A; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<1,2,3,4>> of <<A:5/binary>> -> A; _ -> nomatch end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: unit: resolves to size*unit bits on the read side, byte-aligned and little-endian
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<16#12,16#34>> of <<A:2/unit:8>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<16#12,16#34>> of <<A:1/little-unit:8>> -> A; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<1:1,16#12,16#34>> of <<_:1,A:16>> -> A end end, fun() -> case <<1:1,16#12,16#34>> of <<_:1,A:8,Rest/binary>> -> {A,Rest} end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: an unsized binary/bitstring pattern field takes the rest of the subject at any alignment
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<1,2,3,4>> of <<A:2/binary,Rest/binary>> -> {A,Rest} end end, fun() -> case <<1,2,3,4>> of <<A:3/binary,Rest/bitstring>> -> {A,bit_size(Rest)} end end, fun() -> case <<1,2,3,4>> of <<A:5/binary>> -> A; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<1,2,3:5>> of <<_:21,Rest/bitstring>> -> {bit_size(Rest)} end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a utf16 pattern segment decodes one unit or a surrogate pair, in either byte order
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<16#10000/utf16>> of <<C/utf16>> -> C end end, fun() -> case <<16#10FFFF/utf16-little>> of <<C/utf16-little>> -> C end end, fun() -> case <<255,219,255,223>> of <<C/utf16-little>> -> C end end, fun() -> case <<16#41/utf16>> of <<C/utf16-little>> -> C end end, fun() -> case <<16#41/utf16,65>> of <<C/utf16,Rest/binary>> -> {C,Rest} end end, fun() -> case <<16#41/utf16-native>> of <<C/utf16-native>> -> C end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a utf32 pattern segment decodes one 4-byte code point and leaves the rest of the subject
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<1234/utf32>> of <<C/utf32>> -> C end end, fun() -> case <<16#FF,16#10,0,0>> of <<C/utf32-little>> -> C end end, fun() -> case <<0,0,0,65,255>> of <<C/utf32,Rest/binary>> -> {C,Rest} end end, fun() -> case <<0,0,0,0>> of <<C/utf32>> -> C end end, fun() -> case <<1234/utf32>> of <<C/utf32-signed>> -> C end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a utf32 surrogate or a wrong byte order is a match failure, never a raise
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<0,0,16#D8,0>> of <<C/utf32>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<0,0,16#10,16#FF>> of <<C/utf32-little>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<255,255,255,255>> of <<C/utf32>> -> C; _ -> nomatch end end, fun() -> case <<1234/utf32>> of <<C/utf32>> -> C end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a utf8 pattern segment decodes 1..4 byte sequences and leaves the rest of the subject
cases.eval: try ((fun() -> [F() || F <- [fun() -> case <<16#41/utf8>> of <<C/utf8>> -> C end end, fun() -> case <<16#E0,16#A0,16#80>> of <<C/utf8>> -> C end end, fun() -> case <<16#10FFFF/utf8>> of <<C/utf8>> -> C end end, fun() -> case <<16#E2,16#82,16#AC,65>> of <<C/utf8,Rest/binary>> -> {C,Rest} end end, fun() -> case <<16#F0,16#90,16#80,16#80>> of <<C/utf8>> -> C end end]] end)()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the preloaded `erlang` module is present in the loaded-module registry
cases.eval: try (lists:member(erlang, [Mod || {Mod, _} <- code:all_loaded()])) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the loaded-module registry is at least as large as the preloaded set
cases.eval: try (length([M || {M,_} <- code:all_loaded()]) >= length(erlang:pre_loaded())) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: every code:all_loaded/0 entry is tagged by a module atom, not just the first
cases.eval: try (lists:all(fun(X) -> is_atom(element(1, X)) end, code:all_loaded())) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: every code:all_loaded/0 entry is a two-element {Module,Beam} pair
cases.eval: try (lists:all(fun(T) -> tuple_size(T) =:= 2 end, code:all_loaded())) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: code:all_loaded/0 is a list of {Module, Beam} pairs
cases.eval: try (is_list(code:all_loaded())) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the booted system has at least one loaded module
cases.eval: try (length(code:all_loaded()) > 0) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: every module name projected out of code:all_loaded/0 is an atom
cases.eval: try (lists:all(fun(M) -> is_atom(M) end, [M || {M,_} <- code:all_loaded()])) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: application:get_all_env/1 for kernel is a list of {Key,Value} pairs
cases.eval: try (is_list(application:get_all_env(kernel))) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: application:get_application/0 is `undefined` for a process started outside any application
cases.eval: try (application:get_application()) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: application:get_application/1 resolves a kernel module (`code`) to kernel
cases.eval: try (application:get_application(code)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: application:get_application/1 is `undefined` for a preloaded module outside any application (prim_file)
cases.eval: try (application:get_application(prim_file)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.eval: try (begin Env = application:get_env(kernel), Env =:= undefined orelse (is_tuple(Env) andalso element(1, Env) =:= ok) end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: application:get_env/2 for kernel is `undefined` or {ok,Value} (shape, not a machine value)
cases.eval: try (begin Env = application:get_env(kernel, a_nonexistent_key_xyz), Env =:= undefined orelse (is_tuple(Env) andalso element(1, Env) =:= ok) end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: application:get_env/3 returns the supplied default for an unset key
cases.eval: try (application:get_env(kernel, a_nonexistent_key_xyz, default_value)) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: kernel's `error_logger` env key is unset by the boot script (application:get_env/2 -> undefined)

cases.description: application:get_env/2 reports `undefined` for an unset stdlib key

cases.description: a spawned process computes and sends a value, which the parent receives

cases.description: the parent selectively receives the pid inside a message tuple

cases.description: two processes exchange a request and a reply through the mailbox

cases.description: a process linked across the wire really receives the DOP_EXIT reply: the peer's worker dies 'boom' and the trapping client gets {'EXIT', Pid, boom} whose pid belongs to the peer's node
cases.eval: oracle -noshell -sname dxcli{nonce} -eval try register(dxcli, self()), Peer = list_to_atom("dxpeer{nonce}" ++ lists:nthtail(length("dxcli{nonce}"), atom_to_list(node()))), Pong = case lists:any(fun(_) -> case net_adm:ping(Peer) of pong -> true; _ -> timer:sleep(50), false end end, lists:seq(1, 40)) of true -> pong; false -> pang end, process_flag(trap_exit, true), erlang:send({dxpeer, Peer}, {ask, self()}), M0 = receive X -> X after 10000 -> timeout end, Got = is_tuple(M0) andalso tuple_size(M0) =:= 2 andalso element(1, M0) =:= list_to_atom("worker"), Linked = case Got of true -> erlang:link(element(2, M0)); false -> no_worker end, erlang:send({dxpeer, Peer}, {die_it}), Msg = receive Y -> Y after 20000 -> timeout end, Ok = is_tuple(Msg) andalso tuple_size(Msg) =:= 3, io:format("pong=~p got_worker=~p linked=~p got_exit=~p tag=~p from_peer=~p reason=~p~n", [Pong, Got, Linked, Ok, Ok andalso element(1, Msg) =:= list_to_atom("EXIT"), Ok andalso is_pid(element(2, Msg)) andalso erlang:node(element(2, Msg)) =:= Peer, Ok andalso element(3, Msg)]), halt(0) catch Cls:Rs -> io:format("EXC ~p ~p~n", [Cls, Rs]), halt(1) end. | peer -noshell -sname dxpeer{nonce} -eval try register(dxpeer, self()), timer:sleep(200), io:format("PEER-READY ~p~n", [node()]), W = spawn(fun() -> receive M -> exit(M) after 25000 -> ok end end), receive {ask, From} -> erlang:send(From, {worker, W}) after 25000 -> halt(2) end, receive {die_it} -> erlang:send(W, boom) after 25000 -> halt(2) end, timer:sleep(3000), halt(0) catch Cls:Rs -> io:format("PEEREXC ~p ~p~n", [Cls, Rs]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: with {packet,line} on the accepted socket the client's <<"hello\r\nworld">> yields one {tcp,A,<<"hello\r\n">>} message carrying the EOL, and the unterminated <<"world">> tail delivers nothing (the bounded after answers timeout2)
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{packet, line}, {active, true}]), Sent = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"hello\r\nworld">>), First = receive {tcp, A, D1} -> {data, D1} after 2000 -> timeout1 end, Second = receive {tcp, A, D2} -> {data, D2} after 2000 -> timeout2 end, ok = gen_tcp:close(Cl), ok = gen_tcp:close(A), ok = gen_tcp:close(L), {Sent, First, Second} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: with {packet,4} on the accepted socket the client's <<0,0,0,5,"hello">> bytes are delivered as one {tcp,A,<<"hello">>} message with the four-byte prefix consumed, and inet:getopts/2 echoes the mode
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), SetR = inet:setopts(A, [{packet, 4}, {active, true}]), GetR = inet:getopts(A, [packet]), Sent = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<0, 0, 0, 5, "hello">>), Got = receive {tcp, A, Db} -> {data, Db} after 2000 -> timeout end, ok = gen_tcp:close(Cl), ok = gen_tcp:close(A), ok = gen_tcp:close(L), {SetR, GetR, Sent, Got} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the {packet,4} parser buffers across segments: a lone <<0,0>> truncated prefix delivers nothing, the completing <<0,5,"hello",0,0,0,2,"ab">> delivers <<"hello">> and <<"ab">> as two messages, and the mode is inherited from the listening socket's {packet,4}
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}, {packet, 4}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), GetR = inet:getopts(A, [packet]), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), Partial = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<0, 0>>), Pending = receive {tcp, A, Dp} -> {data, Dp} after 300 -> partial_pending end, Rest = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<0, 5, "hello", 0, 0, 0, 2, "ab">>), First = receive {tcp, A, D1} -> {data, D1} after 2000 -> timeout1 end, Second = receive {tcp, A, D2} -> {data, D2} after 2000 -> timeout2 end, ok = gen_tcp:close(Cl), ok = gen_tcp:close(A), ok = gen_tcp:close(L), {GetR, Partial, Pending, Rest, First, Second} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the read-side framing vocabulary: every named frame parser (raw/line/asn1/sunrm/cdr/fcgi/tpkt/http/http_bin/httph/httph_bin) round trips through the {packet,_} store unchanged with raw normalised to 0, and the numeric forms accept 0..4 while 3/8/16 are {error,einval} and leave the previous mode in place
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, S} = gen_udp:open(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}]), Named = [{T, inet:setopts(S, [{packet, T}]), inet:getopts(S, [packet])} || T <- [raw, line, asn1, sunrm, cdr, fcgi, tpkt, http, http_bin, httph, httph_bin]], Numeric = [{N, inet:setopts(S, [{packet, N}]), inet:getopts(S, [packet])} || N <- [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16]], inet:close(S), {Named, Numeric} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the write-side {packet,N} framing store: 0 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1 round trips through inet:setopts/2 + inet:getopts/2 with the independent {packet_size,N} limit, {packet,17} is {error,einval} and leaves the mode untouched, and gen_udp:open/2 refuses {packet,_} in its option list with badarg
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, S} = gen_udp:open(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}]), M0 = inet:getopts(S, [packet]), Ok4 = inet:setopts(S, [{packet, 4}]), M4 = inet:getopts(S, [packet]), Ok2 = inet:setopts(S, [{packet, 2}]), M2 = inet:getopts(S, [packet]), Ok1 = inet:setopts(S, [{packet, 1}]), M1 = inet:getopts(S, [packet]), Sz0 = inet:getopts(S, [packet_size]), OkSz = inet:setopts(S, [{packet_size, 100}]), Sz100 = inet:getopts(S, [packet_size]), Bad = inet:setopts(S, [{packet, 17}]), AfterBad = inet:getopts(S, [packet]), inet:close(S), OpenPacket = case catch gen_udp:open(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, {packet, 4}]) of {'EXIT', R1} -> R1; {ok, S9} -> inet:close(S9), unexpected_ok; Other -> Other end, {M0, Ok4, M4, Ok2, M2, Ok1, M1, Sz0, OkSz, Sz100, Bad, AfterBad, OpenPacket} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a zero-length passive read armed before the sender fires hands back exactly the arrival ({ok,<<"hello">>}), and the following 2-byte read on the drained socket arms and answers {error,timeout}
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), spawn(fun() -> receive after 500 -> ok end, ok = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"hello">>) end), Rc0 = gen_tcp:recv(A, 0, 2000), Rc2 = gen_tcp:recv(A, 2, 2000), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {Rc0, Rc2} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the pinnable passive-read shape: a spawned sender waits a bounded receive after 500 and only then sends <<"hi">>, so gen_tcp:recv(A,2,2000) is armed before the bytes arrive and answers {ok,<<"hi">>}
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), spawn(fun() -> receive after 500 -> ok end, gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"hi">>) end), Rc = gen_tcp:recv(A, 2, 2000), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), Rc end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: with nothing queued and nothing sent, gen_tcp:recv(A,2,300) arms, lets the caller's bound elapse and answers {error,timeout}; the socket stays open and closeable
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), Rc = gen_tcp:recv(A, 2, 300), Cls = gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(L), {Rc, Cls} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: open_port({spawn_driver,Name},Opts) resolves exactly the statically linked names: tcp_inet/udp_inet/ram_file_drv open live ports whose port_info(P,name) is exactly {name,Name}, while efile and fd raise error:badarg on both runtimes
cases.eval: try ([begin Resp = try open_port({spawn_driver, D}, [binary]) catch error:Reason -> Reason end, case Resp of Bad when is_atom(Bad) -> {list_to_atom(D), Bad}; Pt when is_port(Pt) -> Same = erlang:port_info(Pt, name) =:= {name, D}, true = erlang:port_close(Pt), {list_to_atom(D), Same} end end || D <- ["tcp_inet", "udp_inet", "ram_file_drv", "efile", "fd"]]) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the connected stream's data path: with {active,true} on the accepted socket the client's bytes arrive as one {tcp,S,<<"abc">>} message, and the client's close arrives as the {tcp_closed,S} teardown message
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), ok = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"abc">>), Data = receive {tcp, A, Db} -> {data, Db} after 1000 -> timeout end, ok = gen_tcp:close(Cl), Closed = receive {tcp_closed, A} -> closed after 1000 -> timeout2 end, ok = gen_tcp:close(A), ok = gen_tcp:close(L), {Data, Closed} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the bare tcp driver error matrix: eaddrinuse on a bound local port, enotconn on recv/shutdown of a listening socket, einval on an unknown option, ok on a double close, closed on accept after the close, and badarg on an out-of-range port, a negative port and an unknown listen/connect option
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}]), {ok, P} = inet:port(L), Busy = case gen_tcp:listen(P, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, {reuseaddr, false}]) of {ok, L2} -> gen_tcp:close(L2), ok; Other -> Other end, Recv = gen_tcp:recv(L, 0), Shut = gen_tcp:shutdown(L, read_write), BadOpt = inet:getopts(L, [bogus]), ok = gen_tcp:close(L), Twice = gen_tcp:close(L), Accept = gen_tcp:accept(L), BadPort = case catch gen_tcp:listen(70000, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}]) of {'EXIT', R1} -> R1; {ok, L3} -> gen_tcp:close(L3), unexpected_ok; Other1 -> Other1 end, NegPort = case catch gen_tcp:listen(-5, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}]) of {'EXIT', R2} -> R2; {ok, L4} -> gen_tcp:close(L4), unexpected_ok; Other2 -> Other2 end, BadListenOpt = case catch gen_tcp:listen(0, [bogus]) of {'EXIT', R3} -> R3; {ok, L5} -> gen_tcp:close(L5), unexpected_ok; Other3 -> Other3 end, BadConnOpt = case catch gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, 9, [bogus]) of {'EXIT', R4} -> R4; Other4 -> Other4 end, {Busy, Recv, Shut, BadOpt, Twice, Accept, BadPort, NegPort, BadListenOpt, BadConnOpt} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a loopback gen_tcp:listen(0,[{ip,{127,0,0,1}}]) listener is a live port whose inet:port/1 answers an integer, whose inet:sockname/1 answers the loopback address with the ephemeral port reduced to is_integer/1, whose inet:getopts/2 echoes the {active,true}/{packet,0} defaults, and whose unknown-option query is {error,einval}
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}]), {ok, Pn} = inet:port(L), Sock = case inet:sockname(L) of {ok, {IP, N}} -> {ok, {IP, is_integer(N)}}; Other -> Other end, Opts = inet:getopts(L, [active, packet]), Bad = inet:getopts(L, [bogus]), ok = gen_tcp:close(L), {is_port(L), is_integer(Pn), Sock, Opts, Bad} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: gen_tcp:send/2 answers {error,enotconn} on the listening socket itself and ok on the connected socket a gen_tcp:connect/3 + gen_tcp:accept/1 pair produced
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), ListenSent = gen_tcp:send(L, <<"x">>), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), Acc = case gen_tcp:accept(L) of {ok, A} -> gen_tcp:close(A), accepted; Other -> Other end, ConnSent = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"hi">>), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(L), {ListenSent, Acc, ConnSent} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the bare udp driver error matrix: eaddrinuse on a bound local port, eafnosupport on a wrong-family send, einval on a negative recv length / unknown option, closed on every operation after the close, ok on a double close and badarg on an unknown open option
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, S} = gen_udp:open(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}]), {ok, P} = inet:port(S), Busy = case gen_udp:open(P, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, {reuseaddr, false}]) of {ok, S2} -> inet:close(S2), ok; Other -> Other end, Family = gen_udp:send(S, {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1}, 9, <<"x">>), BadLen = gen_udp:recv(S, -1), BadOpt = inet:getopts(S, [bogus]), ok = inet:close(S), ClosedSend = gen_udp:send(S, {127, 0, 0, 1}, 9, <<"x">>), ClosedRecv = gen_udp:recv(S, 10), ClosedOpt = inet:setopts(S, [{active, false}]), Twice = inet:close(S), BadOpen = case catch gen_udp:open(0, [bogus]) of {'EXIT', Reason} -> Reason; Other2 -> Other2 end, {Busy, Family, BadLen, BadOpt, ClosedSend, ClosedRecv, ClosedOpt, Twice, BadOpen} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: an active-mode datagram sent from a second socket in the same VM is delivered as {udp,S,{127,0,0,1},FromPort,Data} with the sender's ephemeral port reduced to is_integer/1
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, Rd} = gen_udp:open(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, true}]), {ok, RdPort} = inet:port(Rd), {ok, Wr} = gen_udp:open(0, [binary, {active, false}]), Send = gen_udp:send(Wr, {127, 0, 0, 1}, RdPort, <<"abc">>), M = receive {udp, Rd, Ip, From, Db} -> {data, Ip, is_integer(From), Db} after 1000 -> timeout end, gen_udp:close(Wr), gen_udp:close(Rd), {Send, M} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: gen_udp:open/2 on loopback yields a live socket whose {active,_}/{broadcast,_} store round trips through inet:getopts/2 and inet:setopts/2, and which answers {error,einval} to every query once closed
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, S} = gen_udp:open(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}]), {ok, P} = inet:port(S), Dflt = inet:getopts(S, [active, broadcast]), ok = inet:setopts(S, [{active, false}, {broadcast, true}]), Off = inet:getopts(S, [active, broadcast]), ok = inet:setopts(S, [{active, once}, {broadcast, false}]), Once = inet:getopts(S, [active, broadcast]), Sock = case inet:sockname(S) of {ok, {IP, N}} -> {ok, {IP, is_integer(N)}}; Other -> Other end, Cl = inet:close(S), Closed = {inet:getopts(S, [active]), inet:sockname(S)}, {is_port(S), is_integer(P), P > 0, Dflt, Off, Once, Sock, Cl, Closed} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: gen_udp:recv/3 on a passive socket hands back {ok,{Ip,FromPort,Data}} for a datagram a second socket in the same VM sent, with the sender's ephemeral port reduced to is_integer/1
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, Rd} = gen_udp:open(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, RdPort} = inet:port(Rd), {ok, Wr} = gen_udp:open(0, [binary, {active, false}]), ok = gen_udp:send(Wr, {127, 0, 0, 1}, RdPort, <<"hi">>), Rc = case gen_udp:recv(Rd, 0, 1000) of {ok, {Ip, From, Db}} -> {ok, {Ip, is_integer(From), Db}}; Other -> Other end, gen_udp:close(Wr), gen_udp:close(Rd), Rc end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a block framing mode on the sending socket prefixes the frame length: over a fresh connection per mode <<"hello">> is written as <<0,0,0,5,"hello">> under {packet,4}, <<0,5,"hello">> under {packet,2} and <<5,"hello">> under {packet,1}, observed on the raw peer's {active,true} queue with inet:getopts/2 echoing the mode
cases.eval: try (begin Frame = fun(Pk) -> {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}, {packet, Pk}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), Want = 5 + Pk, Drain = fun Loop(Acc) when byte_size(Acc) >= Want -> Acc; Loop(Acc) -> receive {tcp, A, Db} -> Loop(<<Acc/binary, Db/binary>>) after 2000 -> Acc end end, Get = inet:getopts(Cl, [packet]), Sent = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"hello">>), Got = Drain(<<>>), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {Get, Sent, Got} end, [Frame(Pk) || Pk <- [1, 2, 4]] end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the connected pair writes both ways: the client's iolist [<<"pi">>,<<"ng">>] arrives on the accepted socket as <<"ping">> and the accepted socket's <<"pong">> arrives on the client
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), ok = inet:setopts(Cl, [{active, true}]), Up = gen_tcp:send(Cl, [<<"pi">>, <<"ng">>]), AtSrv = receive {tcp, A, D1} -> {data, D1} after 2000 -> timeout1 end, Down = gen_tcp:send(A, <<"pong">>), AtCli = receive {tcp, Cl, D2} -> {data, D2} after 2000 -> timeout2 end, gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {Up, AtSrv, Down, AtCli} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a 256-byte payload holding every byte value 0..255 (list_to_binary(lists:seq(0,255))) is delivered back byte-identical, so the writer escapes and transforms nothing
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), Payload = list_to_binary(lists:seq(0, 255)), N = byte_size(Payload), Drain = fun Loop(Acc) when byte_size(Acc) >= N -> Acc; Loop(Acc) -> receive {tcp, A, Db} -> Loop(<<Acc/binary, Db/binary>>) after 2000 -> Acc end end, Sn = gen_tcp:send(Cl, Payload), D = Drain(<<>>), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {Sn, N, byte_size(D), D =:= Payload, binary:part(D, 0, 4)} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a gen_udp:send/4 on a socket that gen_udp:close/1 closed answers {error,closed} and delivers nothing: the peer's bounded receive answers timeout, so a closed datagram socket puts no datagram on the wire
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, Wr} = gen_udp:open(0, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Rd} = gen_udp:open(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, true}]), {ok, RdPort} = inet:port(Rd), S1 = gen_udp:send(Wr, {127, 0, 0, 1}, RdPort, <<"a">>), G1 = receive {udp, Rd, _, _, D1} -> {data, D1} after 2000 -> timeout1 end, Clo = gen_udp:close(Wr), S2 = gen_udp:send(Wr, {127, 0, 0, 1}, RdPort, <<"b">>), G2 = receive {udp, Rd, _, _, D2} -> {data, D2} after 2000 -> timeout2 end, gen_udp:close(Rd), {S1, G1, Clo, S2, G2} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the datagram writer: gen_udp:send/4 of the iolist [<<"ab">>,<<"cd">>] is one datagram carrying the 4-byte concatenation, a send of <<>> is a deliverable zero-length datagram ({data,<<>>}, not a timeout), and an 8192-byte datagram arrives byte-identical
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, Rd} = gen_udp:open(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, true}]), {ok, RdPort} = inet:port(Rd), {ok, Wr} = gen_udp:open(0, [binary, {active, false}]), S1 = gen_udp:send(Wr, {127, 0, 0, 1}, RdPort, [<<"ab">>, <<"cd">>]), G1 = receive {udp, Rd, _, _, D1} -> {data, D1} after 2000 -> timeout1 end, S2 = gen_udp:send(Wr, {127, 0, 0, 1}, RdPort, <<>>), G2 = receive {udp, Rd, _, _, D2} -> {data, D2} after 2000 -> timeout2 end, Big = binary:copy(<<"0123456789abcdef">>, 512), S3 = gen_udp:send(Wr, {127, 0, 0, 1}, RdPort, Big), G3 = receive {udp, Rd, _, _, D3} -> {size, byte_size(D3), D3 =:= Big} after 2000 -> timeout3 end, gen_udp:close(Wr), gen_udp:close(Rd), {S1, G1, S2, G2, S3, G3} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a zero-length gen_tcp:send/2 on a write-shut socket is still a success (ok, never {error,closed}) and puts nothing on the stream: after gen_tcp:shutdown(Cl,write) the <<>> send answers ok, the peer still receives only the earlier <<"hi">>, and the first non-empty send after it is the {error,closed} refusal
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), Drain = fun Loop(Acc) when byte_size(Acc) >= 2 -> Acc; Loop(Acc) -> receive {tcp, A, Db} -> Loop(<<Acc/binary, Db/binary>>) after 2000 -> Acc end end, Sent = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"hi">>), Shut = gen_tcp:shutdown(Cl, write), Empty = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<>>), S1 = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"x">>), Got = Drain(<<>>), Cls = receive {tcp_closed, A} -> closed after 2000 -> timeout2 end, gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {Sent, Shut, Empty, S1, Got, Cls} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: gen_tcp:send/2 of <<>>, of [] and of [<<>>,[]] all answer ok and put no bytes on the stream: the peer receives only the following <<"hi">>
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), E1 = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<>>), E2 = gen_tcp:send(Cl, []), E3 = gen_tcp:send(Cl, [<<>>, []]), ok = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"hi">>), Got = receive {tcp, A, Db} -> {data, Db} after 2000 -> timeout end, gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {E1, E2, E3, Got} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: with {packet,4} on both ends the header a framed sender writes is consumed by the framed receiver's parser, which hands up exactly <<"hello">> (both option stores echo the mode)
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}, {packet, 4}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{packet, 4}, {active, true}]), GetS = inet:getopts(Cl, [packet]), GetR = inet:getopts(A, [packet]), Sent = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"hello">>), Got = receive {tcp, A, Db} -> {data, Db} after 2000 -> timeout end, gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {GetS, GetR, Sent, Got} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a gen_tcp:send/2 of the deep iolist [<<"ab">>,[$c,$d],[<<"e">>,$f],<<"gh">>] is delivered as the 8-byte concatenation, byte-identical to the same content sent as one flat binary
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), Drain = fun Loop(Acc) when byte_size(Acc) >= 8 -> Acc; Loop(Acc) -> receive {tcp, A, Db} -> Loop(<<Acc/binary, Db/binary>>) after 2000 -> Acc end end, S1 = gen_tcp:send(Cl, [<<"ab">>, [$c, $d], [<<"e">>, $f], <<"gh">>]), D1 = Drain(<<>>), S2 = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"abcdefgh">>), D2 = Drain(<<>>), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {S1, D1, S2, D2, D1 =:= D2} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a 64 KiB payload written by one gen_tcp:send/2 is received in full: the peer drains until the byte count is reached and the row pins 65536 bytes plus the byte sum of the payload the case itself built
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), Payload = binary:copy(<<"0123456789abcdef">>, 4096), N = byte_size(Payload), Drain = fun Loop(Got, Sum) when Got >= N -> {Got, Sum}; Loop(Got, Sum) -> receive {tcp, A, Db} -> Loop(Got + byte_size(Db), Sum + lists:sum(binary_to_list(Db))) after 2000 -> {Got, Sum} end end, Sn = gen_tcp:send(Cl, Payload), {Tot, Ck} = Drain(0, 0), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {N, Sn, Tot, Ck} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: with {packet,line} on the sending socket gen_tcp:send/2 writes the payload unchanged: <<"hi\n">> arrives as those three bytes (EOL included) and <<"nonl">> as those four, with inet:getopts/2 echoing the mode
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), Set = inet:setopts(Cl, [{packet, line}]), Get = inet:getopts(Cl, [packet]), Drain = fun Loop(Acc, Want) when byte_size(Acc) >= Want -> Acc; Loop(Acc, Want) -> receive {tcp, A, Db} -> Loop(<<Acc/binary, Db/binary>>, Want) after 2000 -> Acc end end, S1 = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"hi\n">>), D1 = Drain(<<>>, 3), S2 = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"nonl">>), D2 = Drain(<<>>, 4), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {Set, Get, S1, D1, S2, D2} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the four-byte {packet,4} header is the payload length: a 300-byte payload is written behind <<0,0,1,44>> (a 304-byte frame the peer drains in full), so the prefix is computed, not a fixed constant
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}, {packet, 4}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), Payload = binary:copy(<<"x">>, 300), Want = byte_size(Payload) + 4, Drain = fun Loop(Acc) when byte_size(Acc) >= Want -> Acc; Loop(Acc) -> receive {tcp, A, Db} -> Loop(<<Acc/binary, Db/binary>>) after 2000 -> Acc end end, Sent = gen_tcp:send(Cl, Payload), Got = Drain(<<>>), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {Sent, byte_size(Got), binary:part(Got, 0, 4), binary:part(Got, 4, 2)} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: with {packet,4} applied by inet:setopts(Cl,[{packet,4}]) after gen_tcp:connect/3 the sender still prefixes the four-byte length header, so the framing is read from the live option store rather than from the connect option list
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), ok = inet:setopts(A, [{active, true}]), Set = inet:setopts(Cl, [{packet, 4}]), Get = inet:getopts(Cl, [packet]), Drain = fun Loop(Acc) when byte_size(Acc) >= 9 -> Acc; Loop(Acc) -> receive {tcp, A, Db} -> Loop(<<Acc/binary, Db/binary>>) after 2000 -> Acc end end, Sent = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"hello">>), Got = Drain(<<>>), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {Set, Get, Sent, Got} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the write latch seen from the read side: the first gen_tcp:recv(Cl,0,250) after the failed non-empty write is {error,closed} and the ones after it are {error,enotconn}, so a latched-closed writer closes the reader's answers too — the peer never sent a byte, so no queued input is involved
cases.eval: try (begin {ok, L} = gen_tcp:listen(0, [{ip, {127, 0, 0, 1}}, binary, {active, false}]), {ok, Port} = inet:port(L), {ok, Cl} = gen_tcp:connect({127, 0, 0, 1}, Port, [binary, {active, false}]), {ok, A} = gen_tcp:accept(L), Shut = gen_tcp:shutdown(Cl, write), Pause = fun() -> receive after 40 -> late end end, S1 = gen_tcp:send(Cl, <<"x">>), Pause(), R1 = gen_tcp:recv(Cl, 0, 250), Pause(), R2 = gen_tcp:recv(Cl, 0, 250), Pause(), R3 = gen_tcp:recv(Cl, 0, 250), gen_tcp:close(Cl), gen_tcp:close(A), gen_tcp:close(L), {Shut, S1, R1, R2, R3} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: a second gen_tcp:shutdown(Cl,write) before any send still answers ok (it is idempotent and does not tear the socket down) and the following gen_tcp:send/2 is the same {error,closed} refusal the single-shutdown row pins, with the peer receiving only the pre-shutdown <<"hi">> and its {tcp_closed,A} teardown

cases.description: the half-close's latch: the first non-empty gen_tcp:send/2 after gen_tcp:shutdown(Cl,write) is {error,closed} while every send after it — non-empty or zero-length — is {error,enotconn}, so the failed write moves the socket into a state of its own that a single-send row cannot see

cases.description: maps:from_list/1 (last binding wins), maps:keys/1, values/1, to_list/1 and size/1

cases.description: an absent key anchors ets:next/2 / ets:prev/2 to the neighbouring present keys on both sides of the split, and clamps to '$end_of_table' at the ends
cases.eval: try (begin T = ets:new(ordered_walk_anchor, [ordered_set]), ets:insert(T, [{I,I} || I <- lists:seq(1,100)]), [ets:delete(T, D) || D <- [10,33,70]], Abs = [{ets:next(T, K), ets:prev(T, K)} || K <- [10,33,70]], Edges = {ets:next(T, 0), ets:prev(T, 101), ets:next(T, 1000), ets:prev(T, -1000), ets:next(T, 100), ets:prev(T, 1)}, Other = {ets:next(T, zz), ets:prev(T, zz)}, Present = {ets:next(T, 50), ets:prev(T, 50), ets:next(T, 32), ets:prev(T, 34)}, {Abs, Edges, Other, Present} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: ets:first/1 + ets:next/2 over a >64-key ordered_set whose keys are deleted and inserted mid-walk visits the survivors once, ascending

cases.description: ets:last/1 + ets:prev/2 over a >64-key ordered_set whose keys are deleted and inserted mid-walk visits the survivors once, descending

cases.description: the accepted name set is the twelve BEAM signals — sighup, sigquit, sigabrt, sigalrm, sigterm, sigusr1, sigusr2, sigchld, sigstop, sigtstp, sigcont, sigwinch — and each takes handle and goes back to default, answering ok both times

cases.description: an ERROR reply (truncate on a read-only file) arrives as a proper list of the ERROR response code 1 plus the lowercased errno name eacces
cases.eval: try (begin Pt = open_port({spawn_driver,"ram_file_drv"},[binary]), port_command(Pt, <<1,0,0,0,1>>), _ = receive {Pt,{data,_}} -> ok after 5000 -> timeout end, port_command(Pt, <<14>>), Rep = receive {Pt,{data,D}} -> D after 5000 -> timeout end, Acc = {erlang:is_list(Rep), length(Rep), Rep}, erlang:port_close(Pt), Acc end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.eval: try (begin L = open_port({spawn_driver,"ram_file_drv"},[]), B = open_port({spawn_driver,"ram_file_drv"},[binary]), port_command(L, <<1,0,0,0,3,"abc">>), RL = receive {L,{data,DL}} -> DL after 2000 -> timeout end, port_command(B, <<1,0,0,0,3,"abc">>), RB = receive {B,{data,DB}} -> DB after 2000 -> timeout end, Acc = {RL =:= RB, erlang:is_list(RL), erlang:is_binary(RL), erlang:is_list(RB), RL}, erlang:port_close(L), erlang:port_close(B), Acc end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the port's output counter grows by exactly the command payload: an 8-byte open, then a 3-byte write, read back as {8,11}
cases.eval: try (begin Pt = open_port({spawn_driver,"ram_file_drv"},[binary]), erlang:port_command(Pt, <<1,0,0,0,3,97,98,99>>), A1 = element(2, erlang:port_info(Pt,output)), erlang:port_command(Pt, <<4,120,121>>), A2 = element(2, erlang:port_info(Pt,output)), erlang:port_close(Pt), {A1,A2} end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: port_close/1 answers true once and the second close of the same driver port is badarg

cases.description: port_command/2 accepts a payload for every command word the driver defines (open/read/lseek/write/fsync/truncate/pread/pwrite/fdatasync/get/size/advise/allocate) and answers true for each
port_command/2 to a closed driver port is badarg (the driver is gone, never a silent no-op)
cases.eval: try (begin Pt = open_port({spawn_driver,"ram_file_drv"},[binary]), erlang:port_close(Pt), case catch erlang:port_command(Pt, <<1,0,0,0,0>>) of {'EXIT',{badarg,_}} -> badarg; Other -> Other end end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the C driver's control slot is NULL, so erlang:port_control/3 raises badarg for every opcode — with an empty payload and with a real one
cases.eval: try (begin Pt = open_port({spawn_driver,"ram_file_drv"},[binary]), port_command(Pt, <<1,0,0,0,3,97,98,99>>), _ = receive {Pt,{data,_}} -> ok after 5000 -> ok end, Ops = [0,1,2,3,4,9,14,17,18,19,30,37,38,39], Reasons = lists:usort([case catch erlang:port_control(Pt, Op, Arg) of {'EXIT',{badarg,_}} -> badarg; Other -> Other end || {Op,Arg} <- [{O,<<>>} || O <- Ops] ++ [{37,<<1,2,3>>},{1,<<1,0,0,0,0>>}]]), erlang:port_close(Pt), Reasons end) of V -> io:format("ok ~w~n", [V]), halt(0) catch C:R -> io:format("exception ~w ~w~n", [C, R]), halt(1) end.

cases.description: the whole efile reply matrix round trips: open (NUMBER 0), write abc (NUMBER 3), lseek 1 (NUMBER 1), read 2 (DATA "bc"), lseek 1, truncate (OK), size (NUMBER 1), get (DATA "a") — pinned as the exact reply bytes
